corrected_row: | DOC-A.1-111 | **LEAP-SECOND directive — whether a value greater than 59 seconds may be reported, and the maximum**, §7.3.17.4 GR2 (with §14.9.1.4 GR11, §15.21, §15.99), required + documented | **NO — the seconds position never holds a value greater than 59, with `>>LEAP-SECOND ON` or OFF, so the maximum is 59.** Every reported time comes from the one run-unit clock (`RunUnit.Current.Clock`, a .NET `DateTimeOffset`, which cannot represent a leap second): `ACCEPT … FROM TIME` (`AcceptSource.Time`, seconds in positions 5–6 of HHMMSScc), `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE` (`CobolDate.CurrentDate`) and, from COBOL-2014, `FUNCTION FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE` (`CobolDate.FormattedCurrentDate`), and `FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED`, whose stamp is the compile-time clock reading baked into the program (`ProgramEmitter`). `>>LEAP-SECOND ON` is recognized from COBOL-2002 on (`LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor`) and changes only the ARGUMENT side of the date and time functions, where a seconds value of 60 is accepted — see item 112, which also records that SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT never returns 86,400 or more. | — |

corrected_record.notes: §7.3.17.4 GR2 (cite.py OK §7.3.17.4 2)) leaves to the implementor whether ACCEPT TIME / CURRENT-DATE / FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE / WHEN-COMPILED may report >59 seconds under ON; COBOL.NET answers never. Verified by code reading (AcceptSource.Time uses DateTime.Second; CobolDate.CurrentDate formats RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now(); every temporal source reads IClock -> DateTimeOffset, range 0..59) and probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s4/probe/p111.cob with >>LEAP-SECOND ON and COBOLNET_CLOCK=2016-12-31T23:59:59Z: --std 2014 and 2023 print '59 59 <compile-secs> 59'; p111b.cob at --std 2002 accepts the directive. A 23:59:60 clock pin cannot be expressed (DateTimeOffset.TryParse rejects it), so no test can pin the reported side; Pinned by —. corrected_record.notes: Not written: the line delimiter is implementor-defined (§12.4.5.10.3 GR2, cite.py OK), so CLAUDE.md rule 1 precedence (ISO silent -> GnuCOBOL) governs the choice, and COBOL.NET's differs from GnuCOBOL 3.2's on both sides with no owner decision or CONFORMANCE.md entry recording the deviation. WRITE: SequentialConnector.OpenWriter hard-codes NewLine = "\r\n" on every host; GnuCOBOL 3.2 opens LINE SEQUENTIAL in C text mode (libcob/fileio.c:1894-1899 fmode "w" unless COB_UNIX_LF) and lineseq_write emits '\n' with a '\r' only under cob_ls_uses_cr, which 3.2 never sets (coblocal.h:298, no runtime.cfg entry) - i.e. the host newline, LF on Linux/macOS. READ: ReadPhysicalLine ends a line at a lone CR; GnuCOBOL's lineseq_read (fileio.c:2528-2538) drops CR only before LF and otherwise passes CR through as data. Needs a rule-1 re-determination (or an owner decision recorded in CONFORMANCE.md) before the row is written; golden 2023/pb964_ls_plain_write_after_after pins the CR LF bytes and would move with it.
